players.product: Optical monitors used in optical transceivers, optical filters and attenuators; optical test instruments for optical communications (tunable light sources, optical power meters, connectorized fiber-cable inspection systems)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (April 2025 - March 2026): net sales rose 31.1% on strong sales of optical monitors and optical measuring instruments for optical communications in North America. Gross margin was 57.7%, down 0.7 points on a change in sales mix; SG&A rose on hiring of development staff, higher pay and higher R&D spending; operating margin improved 1.9 points to 32.8%. Average exchange rate JPY 150, in line with plan. Sales by customer location: Japan JPY 7,045,244 thousand, US JPY 10,387,850 thousand, China JPY 5,271,063 thousand, other JPY 8,802,908 thousand. The Other segment (system solutions) grew on expanded sales of ransomware-protection software in Japan
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 31,507 million (+31.1%); operating profit JPY 10,325 million (+39.0%); ordinary profit JPY 10,958 million (+38.9%); profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 7,667 million (+51.3%); gross margin 57.7%; operating margin 32.8%; Other segment sales JPY 2,782 million (+77.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Optical components segment (optical monitors, optical attenuators and optical filters for optical transmission equipment makers; LCOS-based spatial light modulators) for the fiscal year ended March 2026: management states the optical communications market grew strongly with generative AI and data-center investment, and in particular sales of optical monitors used in optical transceivers were strong in North America
quarterly_data.figure: Segment sales JPY 6,356 million (+41.2%); segment profit JPY 1,754 million (+76.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Optical instruments segment (optical communications, industrial and medical instruments) for the fiscal year ended March 2026: sales of connectorized optical fiber cable inspection systems in North America expanded significantly on active generative AI and data-center capex; in China, the special-demand project of the prior year's first half did not recur but customer development kept sales at the prior-year level. Industrial: sales of light sources for medical use and laser-welding inspection in China were firm. Medical: despite a temporary distributor inventory adjustment in Q3, sales of the optical biometer ARGOS, mainly in the US, were firm
quarterly_data.figure: Segment sales JPY 22,368 million (+24.6%); segment profit JPY 8,254 million (+31.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Company targets: the management indicators are a gross margin of 50%, an operating margin of 15% and securing free cash flow. The basic theme for the three years from the fiscal year ending March 2027 to the fiscal year ending March 2029 is creating new customer value through core technologies and group synergy
quarterly_data.figure: Target gross margin 50%; target operating margin 15%

quarterly_data.signal: Management states it expects demand from generative AI and data-center capex in the optical communications market to stay firm, though it has experienced sharp swings in investment trends in the past and its products are constantly exposed to price-reduction pressure. In optical components it will strengthen capex to meet strong demand driven by AI data-center investment and expand market share, and develop new optical components for higher integration, faster communication and lower power; outside communications it is developing spatial light modulators for high-power lasers, mainly for laser processing

Management states that in optical instruments for optical communications it is strengthening stable supply through a factory expansion and relocation and building a production and supply system with lower geopolitical risk; demand for advanced measurement for new technologies supporting AI data centers such as silicon photonics and CPO is rising, and it will launch new products such as a next-generation TSL (tunable light source). In January 2026 it developed the TSL-570 Type U tunable light source for characterization of CPO and silicon photonics devices, from R&D to volume-production evaluation; in March 2026 the TSL-580 tunable light source with a fully redesigned laser cavity and control circuits, and the SPA-200 swept-wavelength photonics analyzer for optical fiber cable assembly inspection and photonics device evaluation (reflection and fault point location, small-loss and waveguide propagation-loss measurement)
quarterly_data.figure: TSL-570 Type U (January 2026); TSL-580 and SPA-200 (March 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: R&D for the fiscal year ended March 2026: group R&D expense JPY 2,534 million (optical components JPY 492 million; optical instruments JPY 2,042 million). Optical components R&D targets small, multifunctional optical components for base stations, data centers and submarine cables; in May 2025 the company developed the SLM-310 spatial light modulator for high-power lasers, with twice the light resistance of its earlier products, for metal 3D printing and precision laser processing. Optical instruments R&D targets new products for silicon photonics and quantum photonics; in medical it is developing the ARGONAUT whole-eye imaging instrument measuring seven key parameters, and it plans a new R&D base in Europe for next-generation medical products. Management expects the semiconductor market, the main outlet for its industrial instruments, to turn from the silicon-wafer capex adjustment toward a gradual recovery
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 2,534 million (optical components JPY 492 million; optical instruments JPY 2,042 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was JPY 1,243 million (including intangibles), mainly equipment for stronger R&D, manufacturing equipment for capacity expansion and production efficiency, plus spending on construction of the new Canada factory; optical components JPY 415 million and optical instruments JPY 647 million. The report lists no significant planned new facilities
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 1,243 million (optical components JPY 415 million; optical instruments JPY 647 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Acquisitions: subsidiary santec LIS acquired all shares of MOG Laboratories (Melbourne, Australia) on July 1, 2025; MOG has developed, made and sold advanced optical instruments mainly for research use in quantum communications and quantum computing since 2007, and was renamed SANTEC AUSTRALIA PTY LTD in May 2026. On June 10, 2026 the company agreed to acquire 500,000 of the 581,400 shares (85.9993%) of HM SOLUTIONS CO., Ltd., acquired on June 19, 2026; HM Solutions has developed, made and sold optical instruments mainly for end-face inspection of optical connectors since 2020, which the company says are highly compatible with its connectorized optical fiber cable inspection systems
quarterly_data.figure: MOG Laboratories all shares (July 1, 2025); HM Solutions 85.9993% (June 19, 2026)
